anomalies.observed: Reference D6 appears twice with two incompatible parts. On the 'LEDs' sheet D6 is a WS2812B addressable pixel in the daisy-chain (D5->D6->D7->D18->D19->D20->D21), with VDD tied to 5V_switched and DIN/DOUT data pins. On the 'LED Enable and E-Stop Config' sheet the same designator D6 is drawn as a discrete LED_RED in the e-stop branch indicator, anode via R27 130R to +3V3 and cathode to the open-drain output of U35 (SN74LVC1G07), i.e. wired as a plain indicator LED, not as a WS2812B. The two sibling indicator LEDs on that sheet are D29 and D28 (three-character refs), so the third column's two-character 'D6' is a reused designator rather than a new part number.
anomalies.expected: Each reference designator must be unique and must match the part it denotes. The specification lists D6 among the WS2812B addressable LEDs ('Addressable status LEDs (WS2812B, D5-D7, D18-D21)' and the board_TODO polarity list 'D5、D6、D7、D18、D19、D20、D21'). The e-stop branch indicator should therefore carry a distinct reference (e.g. D27/D8), not D6.

evidence.quote: LEDs sheet: 'D5 WS2812B' -> 'D6 WS2812B' -> 'D7 WS2812B' chain, D6 VDD to 5V_switched
LED Enable and E-Stop Config sheet: 'LED_RED' with reference 'D6' in series with R27 130R to +3V3, cathode to U35 output (siblings D29, D28)
Addressable status LEDs (WS2812B, D5-D7, D18-D21) ... Make clear the polarity for U5、D19、D5、D6、D20、D7、D21、D18

anomalies.impact: Duplicate designator with two different footprints/types: an ERC/BOM conflict. In assembly, one of the two D6 functions will be mis-populated — either the WS2812B pixel D6 in the status-LED strip is missing/wrong (breaking the LED chain) or the e-stop branch indicator is absent — so board behaviour deviates from the intended design.

parsed.summary: Every component the specification explicitly names (MCP2515 U8/U9, 16 MHz crystals Y1/Y2, isolated CAN transceivers U10/U11, SN74LVC1G07 e-stop/LED buffers, LTC4412 U6, ISL54222 U5/U24, SM712 TVS D9/D10, GLOBAL_EN/SW1) matches the drawing, and the documented known issues (USB diode, GLOBAL_EN sequencing, PoE inversion, C5 footprint) are correctly present. The one deviation the drawing supports is reference D6 being used both as a WS2812B pixel and as a discrete LED_RED e-stop indicator, which contradicts the spec's definition of D6 as a WS2812B and constitutes a duplicate/mismatched component.
